newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Lepanto seen shining on new gold find.
newsitem.headline: Lepanto seen shining on new gold find.

text.p: Lepanto Consolidated Mining Co expects brighter prospects in the next two years, with net income seen rising to one billion pesos in 1998 after its discovery of a new gold mine in northern Philippines, officials said on Monday.
"We will be a major gold producer with our Victoria gold orebody...On its own it's the biggest (gold find in the country)," Lepanto president Artemio Disini told reporters.
The Victoria project in Benguet province is expected to push up Lepanto's net income to at least 648 million pesos this year, company officials said.

The 1997 income forecast was based on prospects that gold prices would fetch an average of $350 per ounce and the exchange rate would stabilise at 26 pesos to a dollar, Lepanto chairman Felipe Yap told shareholders in their annual meeting.
Lepanto posted a consolidated net income of 45.7 million pesos in 1996.
Gold milling from the Victoria ore started on March 16. Lepanto's plant currently has a capacity 1,500 tonnes of ore per day.
"Next year we plan to increase this from 2,000 to 2,500 tonnes per day and (to) 3,000 tonnes in 1998," said Disini.
Disini said Lepanto temporarily shelved production in its adjacent copper mine in Benguet to enable the firm to concentrate its resources on the Victoria gold project.
Lepanto extracted 527,000 ounces of gold from Victoria in its first 15 days of operation.
"A preliminary estimate using drilling and development data with a 30 grams per tonne cut has outlined a mineable reserve of 2.9 million tonnes at 13.6 grams (of gold) per tonne...," Yap said.
"Drilling and development will continue and results are expected to increase the reserves and resources to the potential eight million ounces (of gold)," Yap said.
Lepanto is spending 518 million pesos this year to purchase equipment and other capital expenditures for the development of the Victoria mine, Disini said.
